citation.title: Zero-shot rib design: merging a training-free generative prior with topology optimization

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across 245 runs, 38 of 49 prompt-domain combinations show significant compliance reductions against classical SIMP-based comparison methods; the paper also identifies negative heat-transfer results.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No primary speed-up factor stated in the abstract; the primary comparison is design compliance quality.
claim.alternatives: The conclusion also reports rapid CAD-convertible geometry generation; separate text discusses early compliance signals and search cost, but primary abstract outcome is quality.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP with multi-start and periodic-perturbation baselines; image-guided baseline also included
baseline.implementation: Training-free Stable Diffusion 2.1 prior combined with score distillation sampling; SIMP with Adam optimizer
baseline.solver: Finite element analysis for compliance; Adam density updates
baseline.hardware_classical: CPU/GPU timing resources differ; full hardware detail in timing section not extracted
baseline.hardware_ml: CPU/GPU timing resources differ; full hardware detail in timing section not extracted
baseline.problem_size: 2D plate/design domains across four geometric domains and two physics regimes (Abstract; Methods)
baseline.classical_iterations: Up to study-specific convergence; per-run iteration budgets described in Methods/appendices
baseline.classical_time: Wall-clock costs reported separately; no single value stated in abstract
baseline.ml_time: Wall-clock costs reported separately; no single value stated in abstract
baseline.training_time: No study-specific model training; pretrained Stable Diffusion 2.1 is used, with per-problem score-distillation optimization
baseline.data_generation_cost: No training dataset generated or used (Data availability)
baseline.quality_metric: Finite-element compliance, plus volume constraint and gray-density ratio
baseline.quality_gap: 38/49 prompt-domain combinations significantly improve compliance; median Cohen’s |d|=1.47 (Abstract).

R1.evidence: Abstract: primary outcome compares compliance quality across methods rather than a speed comparison.

R2.evidence: Abstract and Methods: no qualifying inefficient classical baseline marker is established for the primary quality outcome.

R3.evidence: Data availability and Methods: no new training data or offline training; the framework performs per-problem optimization.

R4.evidence: Abstract and Methods: compliance is evaluated by finite-element analysis and volume is enforced, but an aggregate infeasibility/failure rate is not stated.

reporting.n_test_cases: 245 primary score-distillation runs; 49 prompt-domain combinations across four domains and two physics regimes (Abstract).

notes: The diffusion prior is pretrained and publicly available, but implementation code is stated as available on request; no public benchmark code was established.
